title: China Mobile's 'Ling Xi' AI Robotic Guide Dog for the Blind Debuts at AI for Good Summit
detail: Among the assistive-technology demonstrations at the AI for Good Global Summit in Geneva, China Mobile showcased Ling Xi, a phone-controlled robotic guide dog designed to help blind and visually impaired people navigate independently, priced at roughly $4,000 (about €3,500) per unit. The device was displayed alongside other accessibility-focused AI systems at the summit, including a brain-computer interface from Swiss firm Ability Neurotech that enables communication for people with ALS and spinal cord injuries. The demonstrations reflected a broader summit theme: AI-driven assistive devices — from robotic mobility aids to BCIs — moving from research prototypes toward commercially available products for people with disabilities.

title: Robotics for Good Youth Challenge 2026 Grand Finale: Venezuela Sweeps Food-Security Robotics Competition
detail: The ITU's Robotics for Good Youth Challenge 2026 concluded its Grand Finale at the AI for Good Global Summit in Geneva on July 9-10, with teams representing 50 countries across five continents competing in a farm-simulation arena focused on food security. Robots were tasked with irrigation, harvesting ripe fruit, and other practical agricultural missions. Venezuela won first place in both the Junior and Senior categories, with Vietnam taking two second-place prizes. The competition — the leading UN-affiliated global educational robotics championship for students aged 10 to 18 — is designed to have young people build AI- and robotics-based solutions to real-world challenges; the 2026-2027 edition will shift focus to health emergencies in partnership with the World Health Organization.
